summary.headline: Record profits, but mostly one-off Marina Square flat sales: the share prices in far more than the group normally earns
summary.text:
Access Engineering's profit to owners more than doubled to Rs 5.79bn (EPS Rs 5.79) in the six months to September 2026, and the September quarter alone made Rs 4.08 a share. Almost half of it is Marina Square, the 1,088-flat harbour-front development now being handed over, which is sold once; a further Rs 0.44bn is a one-time tax credit. Without them the group earns about Rs 5.1 a share a year, around 9–11% on its equity, well below the 18.6% a shareholder should now demand (beta about 1.0 on Sri Lanka's current risk figures). Debt is high at Rs 39.5bn (0.85x equity) and the business turned little profit into cash over the last two years.

Counting the Marina Square profit still to come (about Rs 9.6 a share in the base case) on top of NAV of Rs 46.70, the three methods give a fair value of about **Rs 34**, against a price of Rs 83.30. I'd buy at up to about **Rs 29** and treat under **Rs 26** as a strong buy. The fair value is lower than the Rs 47 of 9 November mainly because the required return is now worked out from beta (18.6% against 16.5% before) and the methods are tied to book value plus Marina Square. The business tests still fail on returns, one-offs and cash, so it stays in category 3 (avoid for now).

quality.reason: Debt is within the limit, but normal returns are below 15%, recent profit leans on one-offs, and profit hasn't turned into cash.

tests.label: Steady profit: no loss in five years, no one-offs
tests.note: No loss in five years, but each recent year relies on something that won't repeat: a tax credit (2023/24), revaluation gains (2025/26), Marina Square sales and a Rs 0.74bn tax credit (2026/27).

tests.label: Profit turns into cash and dividends
tests.note: Operating cash −Rs 1.26bn and +Rs 0.60bn in 2024/25 and 2025/26 against profit of Rs 13.5bn, as Marina Square and vehicle stock were built; Rs 2.0bn of dividends a year were paid from borrowing. H1 2026/27 cash was Rs 2.75bn as stock fell.

highlights.title: Six months to September 2026: profit up 128%
highlights.text: Revenue Rs 36.97bn (+63%), operating profit Rs 8.92bn (+79%), profit to owners Rs 5.79bn (Rs 2.54bn), EPS Rs 5.79. The September quarter alone: revenue Rs 20.39bn, EPS Rs 4.08 (Rs 1.58).

highlights.title: Marina Square is doing the lifting
highlights.text: Flat handovers brought Rs 8.99bn of revenue and Rs 3.25bn of operating profit (36%) in the half; segment profit Rs 2.81bn, almost untaxed under a BOI tax holiday. Group stock fell to Rs 35.71bn from Rs 43.39bn in March.

highlights.title: One-offs on top
highlights.text: A Rs 0.74bn deferred tax credit at 60%-owned Access Medical Tracers (tax losses from a 100% capital allowance) turned the quarter's tax into a credit. Without Marina Square and that credit, EPS was about Rs 2.54, the same as a year earlier.

highlights.title: Vehicles strong, construction weak
highlights.text: Vehicle revenue Rs 15.46bn (+47%) and segment profit Rs 1.59bn (Rs 0.87bn). Civil engineering profit fell to Rs 0.25bn (Rs 0.64bn) after Rs 1.21bn of allocated finance cost; construction materials fell to Rs 0.24bn (Rs 0.57bn).

highlights.title: Debt still high; cash finally positive
highlights.text: Finance costs more than doubled to Rs 2.57bn. Net debt Rs 39.52bn (Rs 38.87bn in March). Operating cash Rs 2.75bn (−Rs 5.51bn a year earlier) as flats were handed over. Interest cover 4.3x.

highlights.title: After the half-year
highlights.text: The South Asia Commercial and Logistics Hub project (15% stake) is being ended, with about Rs 1.45bn expected back; a share buyback dispute was settled for Rs 225mn (provided for); the Court of Appeal partly upheld a 2011/12 PAYE tax claim of Rs 635mn plus penalties, which the company will appeal.

methodReadings.reading: The price is 1.78x NAV (30 Sep 2026). NAV includes investment property at fair value (Rs 40.8bn) but Marina Square flats at cost, so the flats' profit still to come (about Rs 9.6 a share, base) is added.
Normal ROE about 12% (12.6% in 2025/26 without the revaluation gain), below the 15% test and the 18.6% required return, so book value is worth less than book.

Cheap on reported EPS of Rs 10.42, but about 16x recurring EPS of Rs 5.1. Cross-check: recurring EPS Rs 4.5 / 5.3 / 6.0 × the P/E the returns justify (3.3x / 4.0x / 5.0x) plus Marina Square gives Rs 19 / 31 / 42, close to price to book.
Rs 2.00 a share (Rs 2.0bn) paid in each of the last two years, more than cash after maintenance capex, so funded by borrowing. Not used as a method.

Operating businesses (after-tax operating profit Rs 6.0 / 7.1 / 8.0bn, growth 3/6/9%, return on capital 9–12%) at WACC 15.4/14.4/13.3%, less all net debt: Rs −9.9 / −1.1 / +16.1 a share (84% of the bull value after year 5). The debt also paid for the Marina Square stock (about Rs 28.7bn at cost) and commercial space (Rs 9.3bn), which aren't in the cash flow yet, so this isn't weighted.
Rs 39.52bn at September 2026, interest cover 4.3x. Should fall as Marina Square buyers pay the balance of their flats.

models.name: Adjusted NAV
models.comment: NAV Rs 46.70 plus the Marina Square profit still to come (Rs 4.27 / 9.59 / 12.57), at 0.85x / 1.0x / 1.1x.

models.name: Justified price to book
models.comment: Adjusted book Rs 56.29 (NAV plus base-case Marina Square) × (ROE − growth) ÷ (required return − growth): ROE 10/12/14% against 20.1/18.6/17.1%, so about 0.3–0.7x.

models.name: Residual income
models.comment: Adjusted book Rs 56.29 plus returns above the required return; ROE moves from 10% to 10/12/14% over ten years, payout 35%. Negative while ROE is below the required return.

modelsNote: Three methods, averaged; price to book and residual income from scripts/valuation.py. All three start from book value plus the Marina Square profit still to come, because that profit comes once and would be overstated by any earnings multiple. Growth check: assumed 3% / 6% / 9% a year for five years. The calculator's supported rate (18.4%) is inflated by the Marina Square stock build and the Rs 4.08bn Harbour Village buyout; on ordinary capex alone (Rs 3.24bn booked less Rs 1.26bn depreciation, 29% of after-tax operating profit × 10.5% return on capital) it is about 3%. The base 6% is 3 points above that: the FDG plant is built, the Marina Square commercial space is nearly finished and vehicle demand has reopened. Growth only enters the DCF and P/E cross-checks. The P/E cross-check (Rs 31 base) and the DCF (not meaningful before Marina Square cash comes in) are not weighted.

scenarios.common: NAV Rs 46.70 and net debt Rs 39.52bn at 30 September 2026; 1,000 million shares. Marina Square flats left about Rs 28.7bn at cost (own estimate: Rs 34.43bn in March less about Rs 5.7bn released with H1 sales). Payout 35%. Price Rs 83.30 (CSE close, 20 November 2026).

sensitivity.title: Fair value (three methods), Rs per share
sensitivity.note: Bear and bull move with the base (±1.5 points of required return, ±2 points of ROE). Even at a 14% required return and 16% ROE for good, the methods give about Rs 63, below today's Rs 83.30. The price assumes Marina Square is worth far more than its remaining cost plus 30%, or that the group's returns jump well above anything it has earned without one-offs.

buyPlan.note: About Rs 15,075 in total, against Rs 41,650 at Rs 83.30.
buyPlan.realism: Not realistic in normal markets: Rs 34.26 is 59% below the price. The share has traded between Rs 66.90 and Rs 80.60 since April 2026 and was last near Rs 34 in April 2025 (low Rs 34.80). Owning it at these prices would take a broad market fall or a Marina Square disappointment; otherwise it means waiting for normal returns to rise well above 15%.

fullText:
**Access Engineering PLC (AEL.N0000): analysis of 20 November 2026**

**Summary.** Profit to owners for the six months to September 2026 was Rs 5.79bn (EPS Rs 5.79, up from Rs 2.54), and the September quarter alone made Rs 4.08 a share. Most of the jump is Marina Square, the 1,088-flat harbour-front development whose flats are now being handed over: Rs 8.99bn of revenue and Rs 2.81bn of profit in the half, almost untaxed under a BOI tax holiday. A one-time Rs 0.74bn deferred tax credit at Access Medical Tracers added more. Without them the group earned about Rs 2.54 a share, the same as a year earlier, or roughly Rs 5.1 a year: around 9–11% on equity, against a required return of 18.6%.

At Rs 83.30 the share trades at 1.78x NAV (Rs 46.70) and 8x trailing EPS, but about 16x recurring EPS. The three methods, each counting the Marina Square profit still to come, give a fair value of **Rs 34.26**, buy price **Rs 29.12** and strong-buy price **Rs 25.70**. Verdict: overpriced. Business tests: 1 of 4 passed (debt), so category 3, avoid for now (unchanged).

**What changed since 9 November.** Fair value Rs 47.0 → Rs 34.26. The required return is now built from beta (1.01, provisional) and the shared market inputs: 18.6% base instead of 16.5%. The P/E method was dropped from the average because Marina Square's one-off profit can't be capitalised at a multiple; justified price to book and residual income now start from NAV plus the Marina Square value. NAV rose to Rs 46.70 with the half-year's profit.

**The business.** Nine segments: civil engineering, construction materials, mechanical engineering (port equipment), commercial offices and warehouses (investment property at fair value, Rs 40.8bn), condominiums (Marina Square), renewable energy (15.85 MW rooftop solar), vehicles (Isuzu through 84%-owned Sathosa Motors, Jaguar Land Rover through Access Motors) and radiopharmaceuticals (60%-owned Access Medical Tracers, Sri Lanka's first FDG cyclotron plant). Harbour Village, which owns Marina Square, became 100% owned in 2025/26 for Rs 5.6bn.

**Latest results (six months to 30 September 2026, unaudited).** Revenue Rs 36.97bn (+63%); operating profit Rs 8.92bn (+79%); finance costs Rs 2.57bn (Rs 1.09bn); profit to owners Rs 5.79bn. Vehicles: revenue Rs 15.46bn, segment profit Rs 1.59bn (Rs 0.87bn). Civil engineering: segment profit Rs 0.25bn (Rs 0.64bn) after Rs 1.21bn of allocated finance cost. Construction materials Rs 0.24bn (Rs 0.57bn). Operating cash Rs 2.75bn as stock fell to Rs 35.71bn from Rs 43.39bn. Net debt Rs 39.52bn. NAV Rs 46.70.

**Year to March 2026 (audited).** Revenue Rs 49.66bn (+44%), profit to owners Rs 7.17bn (EPS Rs 7.17), including a Rs 4.01bn fair value gain on investment property; about Rs 5.12 a share without it. Operating cash only Rs 0.60bn as Rs 18.3bn more went into stock (mainly Marina Square). Borrowings rose to Rs 42.5bn from Rs 27.6bn. Dividend Rs 2.00 a share.

**Marina Square.** Flats were on the books at Rs 34.43bn of cost in March 2026, and buyers had paid Rs 20.2bn of advances (group). About Rs 5.7bn of cost was released with the half-year's sales, so roughly Rs 28.7bn remains (own estimate; the reports don't give units sold or unsold). At a 30% margin after finance cost, untaxed, over about three years, the remaining profit is worth about Rs 9.6 a share today (bear Rs 4.3: 20% margin, some tax, four years; bull Rs 12.6: 34%, two years). The commercial space (Rs 9.3bn at cost, investment property under construction) isn't counted; it may bring a revaluation gain and rent once let.

**Required return.** Cost of equity 8.24% + 1.01 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 18.6% (bear 20.1%, bull 17.1%). Beta: segments weighted by operating profit (property 48%, construction 26%, vehicles 25%, renewables 2%), Damodaran sector betas from web-search extracts (his emerging-markets file couldn't be opened), unlevered 0.76, relevered at net debt 0.47x market value: 1.01. No local beta could be found. Cost of debt 8.1% (interest paid ÷ average debt), WACC 14.4%, used only in the DCF cross-check.

**Methods (Rs a share, bear / base / bull → weighted 30/50/20).**
- Adjusted NAV: 43.32 / 56.29 / 65.20 → 54.18. NAV plus Marina Square, at 0.85x / 1.0x / 1.1x.
- Justified price to book: 18.64 / 26.80 / 39.01 → 26.79. Adjusted book Rs 56.29 × (ROE − g) ÷ (r − g), ROE 10/12/14%, growth 5/6/7%.
- Residual income: 15.73 / 21.68 / 31.28 → 21.82. Starts at 10% ROE, payout 35%.
- Fair value: average Rs 34.26.
Cross-checks, not weighted: P/E (recurring EPS Rs 4.5 / 5.3 / 6.0 × justified P/E 3.3x / 4.0x / 5.0x, plus Marina Square) Rs 19 / 31 / 42; whole-company DCF of the operating businesses Rs −9.9 / −1.1 / +16.1 before counting the Marina Square stock that the debt paid for (84% of the bull value after year 5).

**Growth and reinvestment.** 2025/26 capex booked Rs 3.24bn against depreciation Rs 1.26bn; Rs 1.89bn of it was the FDG plant (growth), so maintenance spending is close to depreciation. The calculator's supported growth (18.4%) is inflated by the Marina Square stock build and the Harbour Village buyout; on ordinary capex it is about 3%. Assumed growth 3% / 6% / 9%; the base is 3 points above that, justified by the FDG plant, the Marina Square commercial space and vehicle demand. Dividends (Rs 2.0bn) were more than cash after maintenance capex in both years, so they were partly borrowed: at risk if Marina Square cash is slow.

**Earnings run-rate.** Reported run-rate is far higher (12 months Rs 10.42; September quarter × 4 Rs 16.32) but includes Marina Square flat sales, which end when the flats are sold, and the one-time tax credit. Recurring EPS of about Rs 5.1 is the base for the P/E cross-check.

**Ratios outside the normal range.** Net debt is about 3.5x EBITDA without revaluation gains (above 3x) because the debt also carries the Marina Square stock; it should fall as flats are paid for. Cost of debt (8.1%) is about 4 points below the bond yield: bank loans repriced as lending rates fell in 2025/26.

**Business tests.** Returns: fail (normal ROE about 12%). Debt: pass (0.85x equity). Steady profit: fail (no loss, but one-offs every recent year). Cash: fail (operating cash negative over two years against Rs 13.5bn of profit). 1 of 4: weak, category 3.

**Management.** The plan is to finish Marina Square, sell the remaining flats and lease the commercial space, while growing logistics warehousing, port engineering and radiopharmaceuticals. The stated prudent, internally funded approach wasn't borne out in 2025/26 (borrowings up Rs 14.9bn), and the 15% logistics-hub investment is being ended with about Rs 1.45bn expected back.

**Shareholders.** Founders control the company: the Perera family about 30%, the Joshua family about 19%, three other founding directors 3% each. The Employees' Provident Fund raised its stake to 5.69% (from 3.21% in March and 4.33% in June). Public holding 38.29%.

**Buy plan (500 shares).** 200 at up to Rs 34.26, 150 at up to Rs 29.12, 150 at up to Rs 25.70: about Rs 15,075 in all (average Rs 30.15). Not realistic at today's prices: the share hasn't been below Rs 66.90 since April 2026.

**What to watch.** Marina Square sales, margins and how many flats remain; whether debt falls; construction order book and new contracts; vehicle demand; the PAYE tax appeal (Rs 635mn plus Rs 317mn penalties claimed); the end date of the BOI tax holiday.
